<span id="before-you-write"></span>
== Before you write ==

# '''Confirm eligibility first.''' Read the funder’s eligibility page. Do they need a legal entity or tax-exempt status? A fiscal sponsor (see [[Fiscal sponsorship]]) may be needed.
# '''Confirm the funder is active.''' Some funders have closed or stopped taking unsolicited applications.
# '''Match their scope.''' A fund for internet infrastructure will not want a user-facing app. Pitch the part of your work that fits.
# '''Note the deadline''' and the maximum first-proposal amount.

<span id="a-proposal-skeleton"></span>
== A proposal skeleton ==

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Section
! What goes in it
|-
| Problem
| Who is harmed by the status quo, with evidence (per-seat pricing, lock-in, export walls)
|-
| Solution
| What you built or will build, and what is already working (demo rather than promise)
|-
| Why you
| Track record, public repositories, certifications such as the OpenID certification of [[ZeroAuthy]]
|-
| Plan and milestones
| Scoped work, each step checkable
|-
| Budget
| Hours, rates, infrastructure, and the fee if you use a sponsor
|-
| Risks
| Honest list: maturity, clean-room safety, bus factor
|-
| Outcomes
| What the public gets, measured by compatibility tests passing, releases, adopters
|}

<span id="tips"></span>
== Tips ==

* Lead with what already runs. Say plainly what is planned versus shipped.
* Keep the clean-room method and provenance front and centre: it answers legal worries.
* Use the funder’s own words for their goals.

<span id="where-to-find-funders"></span>
== Where to find funders ==

* '''Foundation Directory Online:''' free through participating public libraries, paid otherwise. Check whether a library near you participates.
* '''GrantStation:''' a subscription database; it is cheaper through a non-profit association or TechSoup, which runs an annual sale.
* '''GrantStation weekly newsletter:''' free, covers grantmaker news and deadlines.
* '''Bank philanthropy programs''' (for example Bank of America, Wells Fargo, TD Bank, Chase, Capital One): worth checking starting with banks in your area.
* See [[Non-profit funding sources]] for open source funders.
